data.title: ‘You have to be careful, to go slow & fast’: Inside high-risk mission at International Space Station
data.description: Mark Owen is pleased to welcome Michel Tognini, former head of the European Astronaut Centre of the European Space Agency. Tognini sees a spacewalk as a paradox of human spaceflight: from the ground, it can look almost effortless, but outside the space station, even the simplest movement takes place within an exceptionally unforgiving environment. Sophie Adenot’s EVA demands constant attention to her suit, her tether, her tools, her route around a structure roughly the size of a football pitch, and the dramatic temperature changes between sunlight and darkness. For Tognini, the essential discipline of a spacewalk is simple to describe but extremely challenging to master.

data.title: Ebola in DRC: Deadliest outbreak on record ‘outpacing the response’
data.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome WHO Spokesperson Tarik Jašarević. His central concern is that we do not yet know where all the places the Ebola virus is circulating: infected people remain outside treatment centres, transmission chains go undetected, and patients who seek care too late face much poorer chances of survival. Conflict, population mobility and other humanitarian pressures make surveillance more difficult, but community engagement is equally crucial. Without trust and cooperation, testing, contact tracing, safe burials and early treatment cannot work effectively.

data.title: The flag culture wars have come to an unlikely place: progressive Iceland | Alexander Hurst
data.description: Ahead of the Nordic nation’s EU referendum, the Icelandic flag has been co-opted by the far right To enter Reykjavik’s Grafarvogur Lutheran church, worshippers and visitors are invited to make their way down 16 steps painted in the rainbow stripes and the white, pink, blue, brown and black chevrons of the Progress Pride flag. The artwork, which can even be seen on satellite pictures, was originally a project of former head pastor Guðrún Karls Helgudóttir, now the bishop of Iceland, and her colleagues. The point was to show support for the LGBTQ+ community’s “need to be visible and accepted”, the church’s current head pastor , Arna Sigurðardóttir, told me. And then some time in between the barely faded midnight sun of 7 July and the early morning light of 8 July, someone painted over all those colours with just three: blue on the outside, and two thin strips of white encasing a thicker strip of red in the centre. Continue reading...

data.title: Brain-breaking sex, bad boys in leather and queer glory: why TV vampires are so intoxicating
data.description: The Vampire Lestat has seduced fans around the world with his eye-popping antics. But this obsession with hot vamps goes way beyond forbidden love, bare chests and a taste for LSD-laced blood If you want TV audiences to forgive a fictional man for absolutely anything, just sharpen his fangs and stick him in velvet. Case in point? The horny musical drama The Vampire Lestat, which became a cult hit in the US earlier this year. The show has now arrived in the UK and Sam Reid’s searing performance as Lestat has fans on their knees. The first two seasons, which went by the title Interview With the Vampire, were about the “interview” in which Louis (Jacob Anderson) tells a journalist about his toxic relationship with Lestat. Now, the focus has shifted to Lestat – hence the new title and new narrator – as the golden-locked prince of darkness swaps centuries of secrecy for glam-rock stardom. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Our task is to laugh at these enemies’: the Ukrainian unit posting drone videos of Russian soldiers’ last moments
data.description: Creators of chase compilations reject any moral qualms and say they show ‘death is waiting’ for those who join war To many observers they will appear dehumanising and offensive. To many Ukrainians, however, they are a brutal reminder of the fate that awaits Russian soldiers who take part in Vladimir Putin’s invasion, as well as a potent propaganda weapon. Over the past year and a half, videos of kamikaze drones chasing Russian service personnel to their deaths have become a distinctive genre on social media. They are the brainchild of Robert Brovdi , the head of Ukraine’s unmanned systems forces and founder of “Magyar’s Birds” , named after his call sign. Continue reading...

data.title: Where on earth is Melania Trump? | Arwa Mahdawi
data.description: In her husband’s first term, her absences sparked conspiracy theories. This time, she is somehow keeping an even lower profile Anyone seen a 56-year-old woman around lately? Tall, cinnamon blond hair, fond of a fancy hat and, to quote Vogue , occasionally dresses like a “freelance magician”. She goes by the name “Melania Trump” or “first lady”, and she appears to be missing again. According to an analysis by the Daily Beast , Melania has only made 38 public appearances this year – with the last being the World Cup final. She’s been MIA for about a month. To be fair, this isn’t out of character. During her first stint in the White House, the first lady’s frequent absences sparked various conspiracy theories, including one that she had a body double . But it seems Melania is keeping an even lower profile during Trump 2.0. NBC reported on Monday that she’s done about half as many public events as she did at this point in Trump’s first term. A senior adviser told the outlet she “prioritises results over appearances”. I dunno about that. Her highest-profile public appearance this year was when she held a surprise press conference telling everyone not to speculate about her relationship with Jeffrey Epstein. This had the predictable result of getting everyone to speculate about her relationship with the dead sex offender. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: I’m 50 years old. Why do I still struggle with the need to be liked?
data.description: An over-investment in people-pleasing can be emotionally costly. Here’s how I’m training myself to be OK with letting people down A few months ago, my 10-year-old daughter and I went to our neighborhood cafe. At the counter, the owner greeted us with her typical effusion of warmth and welcome. Instead of greeting her in kind, my daughter looked on with a stony expression and ungiving eyes. My face flushed. I was embarrassed and incensed by what I perceived as blatant rudeness. You could at least smile, I thought. Continue reading...

data.title: Carbon pollution has fuelled ‘massive expansion’ of marine heatwaves in Europe, study finds
data.description: Hottest periods this year in most sea regions would have been ‘virtually impossible’ in a preindustrial climate Carbon pollution has fuelled a “massive expansion” of marine heatwaves in Europe this summer, research has found, with some waters recording temperatures 6C higher than normal. The hottest fortnights of this year would have been “virtually impossible” in a preindustrial climate in three of the four sea regions studied, according to analysis by World Weather Attribution , while in the Celtic region, which covers much of the water around the British Isles, heat hit levels that used to strike just once a century. Continue reading...

data.title: The Great ADHD Myth? review – the most controversial show of the year is here
data.description: Dr Max Pemberton isn’t uncompassionate or especially radical, but he assembles a team of medics whose stance on the condition is clear from the off. This is a documentary that will incense and offend many Presenter Max Pemberton, a psychiatrist in the NHS, Daily Mail columnist and author, and the experts he has assembled, waste no time in setting out their stall in The Great ADHD Myth?. This is a documentary that will incense and offend some of its viewers, and its scepticism regarding ADHD is clear from the outset. “It’s certainly not a medical condition as far as I’m concerned,” says the former president of the Royal College of General Practitioners, Dr Iona Heath. “We’re going to look back and think: did we actually put a chemical cosh on an entire developing generation of brains?” says a neurophysiological psychologist. “The industry around ADHD is about making money at the cost of the misery of others,” says a former president of the Royal College of Psychiatrists. These represent the three main questions raised by Pemberton. The first is whether ADHD is a neuro-developmental disorder – ie do those diagnosed with the condition have different brains from those without – or whether it is a way of suppressing natural tendencies (especially those of children) and inducing behaviours that society deems acceptable. The second is how doctors should approach treatment, which most often involves amphetamines. “These are controlled drugs,” says consultant child and adolescent psychiatrist Dr Sami Timimi. “There’s good reason why we warn the rest of the population [about them].” The third question is – who benefits from the increase in diagnoses we have seen in the past decade or so? How has ADHD moved from a relatively unknown condition 10 years ago to affecting about 2.5 million people in the UK today (including a 200% increase in people being referred for diagnosis in the past five years)? Continue reading...

data.title: Little Bird review – no wonder this masterly drama has already cleaned up awards
data.description: It’s impossible not be be enraged by this story of Indigenous children who were taken from their families. This heartbreaking show has been a hit in Canada – and it would be a crime for the rest of the world to miss it Few dramas will enrage you as much as Little Bird. Not because it’s in any way hokey or problematic. On the contrary. Based on the real story of the Sixties Scoop – a period in Canada from the mid-1950s to the 1980s, when an estimated 20,000 First Nations children were forcibly removed from their families and adopted by non-Indigenous families – this heartbreaking tale is restrained and carefully measured. Melodrama is swerved, letting the injustice at this story’s core slowly metastasise. Spread across six episodes, the series juggles two timelines – 1968 in Saskatchewan; 1985 in Montreal – tracking one family’s rupture; and the decades-long reckoning that follows. We meet Esther Rosenblum (Darla Contois), a first-year law student, at her engagement party, where her fiance David (Rowen Kahn), a doctor, mingles with his wealthy Jewish family. When his mother describes her as “exotic”, the word lodges like shrapnel. She was transplanted when she was five from the (fictional) and raised in the Jewish faith by a Canadian family. Little Bird aired on Sky Atlantic and is on Now in the UK and on Stan in Australia Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Even its loos are on the outside’: hi-tech, inside-out marvel the Lloyd’s building is partying with the public
data.description: It has been likened to a monster, an oil rig – and the Parthenon. Now, for its 40th birthday, the astonishing London landmark has joined the Open House festival, to grant admirers a rare look around the inside In his 2012 book A New Kind of Bleak, the critic Owen Hatherley called it “monstrous, compelling” and utterly messed-up. Back in the 1980s, a then Prince Charles suggested it had been inspired by a North Sea oil rig. But none of this stopped it from becoming, in 2011, the youngest ever building to be given Grade I-listed status in the UK. And now, as part of its 40th anniversary celebrations, the Lloyd’s building will open to the public for the first time since 2014 for one day only during London’s Open House festival. The iconic building in the heart of the financial district was designed by architect Richard Rogers to house the global insurance marketplace. Its futuristic facade has been a celebrated part of the City of London skyline since it opened in 1986, but the interior is rarely seen by the public. Visitor galleries with a view of the trading floor have long been shut for security reasons. Continue reading...

data.title: Dickovers, baggravation and botiquette: 18 new words to describe our tech hellscape
data.description: There are many tech irritants that are a scourge of modern life, yet we have lacked the vocabulary to describe them ... until now The “dickover” is the scourge of the modern age. Coined in May by John Gruber, a tech writer, it is defined as “a modal panel, popover, or curtain presented by a website or app, deliberately obscuring its own content to frustrate the user”. Essentially, it is the thing (or more often, things) you have to click away in order to read the thing you wanted to read. It is the “accept cookies” box, the “allow notifications?” box, the “sign in with Google” box, the pop-up video box, etc. We shouldn’t fool ourselves into thinking that dickovers are the only terrible thing about technology in 2026. Until now, though, we have lacked the vocabulary to describe them, so here are some suggestions. Continue reading...

data.title: Introducing Ulez was my hardest decision as mayor of London – but now we know its astonishing impact | Sadiq Khan
data.description: Critics said I was attacking motorists. It’s more important for me that the city’s children are no longer breathing dangerous levels of pollution Ulez led to better lung size and function among London children, study finds When I introduced London’s clean air zone – the ultra-low emission zone (Ulez) – more than seven years ago, no city had ever attempted anything quite like it. At the time, the scheme in central London provoked fierce opposition. When I decided to expand it – first in 2021, to inner London, and then again in 2023 to the whole city, making it the biggest clean-air zone in the world – my detractors were louder still. I had, they claimed, declared war on drivers in blind pursuit of a policy that may not even work. All the mainstream political parties, including my own, were opposed. In recent years, though, those critics have gone quiet. There is now a mountain of evidence to show that the Ulez has slashed air pollution and improved air quality across London, and research published by Imperial College London earlier this year showed that this is already saving lives. Between 2019 (when I first introduced the Ulez) and 2024, estimated deaths associated with air pollution in the capital fell by around 40%. But a new, independent study published by Queen Mary University of London today goes further still, showing how – by helping to clean up the capital’s air – the Ulez is improving the lungs and lives of London’s children. Sadiq Khan is mayor of London Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: Here is the news from the US: Woke 1.0 is over. But what did progressives do wrong? | Nesrine Malik
data.description: A movement with safety, dignity and equality at its heart may now be blamed for the rightwing backlash. But within it were principles worth carrying forwards Every once in a while, the discourse gods send a tablet down to the people, announcing that a previous era is dead and a new age is upon us. Recently, it was the “ vibe shift ” – a post-pandemic change in culture that encompassed everything from fashion to politics. The vibe shift consolidated with Donald Trump’s second election, a harbinger of the end of fragility and of movements for racial and gender equality – a rejection of the long 2010s with their hashtags and pink pussy hats and women’s marches and protests. The vibe shift has recently been followed by a calling of time on what has come to be known as “Woke 1.0” – a term that represents what is now seen as a culture of hysterical overreach triggered by the momentary breakthrough of movements such as #MeToo and Black Lives Matter. “Woke 1 was crazy,” said Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez this month, quoting a New York City councilman. And there we have it, time to walk back some things said and done in the giddy heat of those moments. It was crazy! This rush to the future away from what some perceive to be an embarrassing past groups together various disparate phenomena. But I’m afraid it’s not that simple. Woke 1.0 (or “peak wokeness” – I wish the gods would use less trivialising ways to refer to roiling social tides, but there we are) was about politics and culture and also about the behaviours and trends it triggered. It was about concrete problems: policing of minority communities, the right of women not to be sexually harassed or violated, the systemic racism and sexism that damaged both. And it was about reforming the cultural structures that created and perpetuated those systems; asking university curricula to expand and diversify intellectual sources, recognising the long shadow of glorified imperial histories, and updating institutions – from the media to the academy – in order to enfranchise change. None of this is “crazy”. Nesrine Malik is a Guardian columnist Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: Barcelona steal Rodri away from Real Madrid and plan to make him new Busquets
data.description: Spain’s World Cup-winning captain has completed his move to Camp Nou where he is a natural successor to club legend By the time Flight PTN27B started its descent into El Prat a bit before 8pm on Monday evening, a small crowd had gathered by the terminal doors, waiting for it to land. A few people stood and watched the sky, cameras out to capture its arrival. A lot more watched on their phones. In the two hours it had taken to get there from Manchester, taking off at 5.11pm, 101 minutes behind schedule, the Pilatus PC-24 had become the most tracked plane on the planet. Everyone knew that Rodrigo Hernández was on board. Unless, of course, he had been sneaked away in a catering cart. Five days earlier, Rodri had been seen, and recorded, at Barajas airport waiting to get on a flight back to Manchester from Madrid. He wheeled a small RFEF (Spanish football federation) case with his name on, stood alone in the queue, the World Cup-winning captain just a bloke in shorts and T-shirt, and his stay in the UK was supposed to be brief, just long enough to say goodbye. The plane he was boarding was a Ryanair one: that was the detail everyone homed in on, something extraordinary in the ordinariness. This time, though, he came on a private jet, one way. His family travelled with him. He came to sign for FC Barcelona. Continue reading...

data.title: Interviewing José Mourinho: ego, charisma, talent and his ‘rucksack of pain’
data.description: Director Joe Pearlman says he expected Real Madrid manager to ‘try to manipulate us’ in making of Netflix series Even in the hyperreal world of football, there are few characters more compelling, more polarising, or more everything than José Mourinho, the best and worst of public him on full display in a new three-part Netflix series . “It reminded me how good he was,” says Joe Pearlman, who directed Mourinho, and the actual Mourinho is, believe it or not, keen to communicate the same. As he puts it in the show: “I look, you look, I see more than you.” Making documentaries, though, is often about taking people to the places they’re most skilled at avoiding. “I knew the interviews were going to be very intense,” says Pearlman, “and he was going to try and control the narrative and manipulate us. Everything bad is everyone else’s fault and everything he’s done is validated by winning. Because that’s all that’s important.” Continue reading...

data.title: US states accuse Meta of covering up research on teen social media addiction in pivotal trial
data.description: State attorneys general claim tech company intentionally designed addictive products that harm young people Lawyers representing 29 US states have accused Meta of covering up internal research showing Instagram was addictive for teenagers. In a packed courtroom Tuesday, on the opening day of a landmark legal challenge, they said the company knew its products harmed children but hid that information from the public. “I heard from many of you at jury selection that the health and wellbeing of kids is a shared responsibility,” said Megan O’Neill, a deputy attorney general for California, in her opening statements. “Meta didn’t do its share.” Continue reading...

data.title: ‘We humans are inept at taking care of baby animals’: why well-fed orphan bears die in the wild
data.description: Scientists surprised to find all but two of 12 grizzlies were dead within a year of ‘feelgood’ release, unable to sustain their high-calorie diet and inclined to approach humans The orphaned grizzly bear cubs were bulked up with a generous diet of roadkill, watermelon, dog food and snacks donated by the public. Their contact with carers was limited to two people. Then, after up to a year in rehabilitation, they returned home to the wilds of British Columbia. “It’s a feelgood thing – people feel good when the cage opens,” says Dr Lana M Ciarniello, a bear specialist who tracked the Canadian yearlings in a recent study . There is a perception that bears will thrive in their natural habitat, she says. “The reality is they’re not followed up on.” Continue reading...

data.title: England’s ancient oak trees dying in extreme hot and dry weather
data.description: Woodland Trust says trees struggling in drought stress, with older ‘survivors’ disproportionately affected England’s ancient oak trees are dying in the summer’s extreme heat and dry weather, according to the Woodland Trust, with trees and ecosystems unable to adapt fast enough to the changing climate. The heatwaves across much of Europe this summer have had a notable impact on crop growth and plant health. To cope with the extreme conditions, many trees are undergoing “early autumn”, wilting and losing their leaves early. Crow Leasow oak, Shropshire. Tea Party oak, Suffolk. King John oak, Devon. Enmore oak, Somerset. Lydham Manor oak, Shropshire. Old Knobbley, Essex. Pwllpriddog oak, Carmarthenshire. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘A new normal’: Miami faces worsening seaweed problem as piles of algae wash up on beaches
data.description: Officials have had to remove thousands of tons of sargassum from Florida’s beaches amid the climate crisis Dealing with seaweed is the bulk of Chris Bumpus’s job during the summer. As chief of conservation for Miami-Dade county’s parks, recreation and open spaces department, Bumpus is in charge of cleaning sargassum off 17 miles (27km) of county beaches. But some days, the odds are stacked against him and his team. More and more sargassum, a kind of floating brown algae, has been washing up on the beaches of south Florida, west Africa, the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘There was a certain hostility’: how Wet Hot American Summer went from miss to hit
data.description: Critics might have been sniffy back in 2001 but the silly summer camp comedy has endured and director David Wain has been enjoying the ‘slow-burn’ appreciation In the summer of 2001, the film critic Roger Ebert wrote a scathing film review in song form, with lyrics set to the tune of a classic song about summer camp. “ Hello muddah, hello fadduh / Here I am at Wet Hot American Summah,” it began. The review proceeded to mock the film Wet Hot American Summer in rhyme. Twenty-five years later, the film’s director and co-writer, David Wain, joined several of its stars on the vast lawn of the Autry Museum in Los Angeles to sing the review to a crowd of thousands, many of them wearing Camp Firewood T-shirts and 80s-style sweat absorbers. The performance preceded an anniversary screening of what has become a cult classic. Continue reading...

data.title: Match review – gory and slyly satirical catfishing horror for the age of Hinge
data.description: Online dating’s eternal bugbear reaches a horrific apotheosis in this funny, grimy and impishly directed shocker Paola (Humberly González) is a pretty young woman about to turn 30 who hasn’t found herself a steady boyfriend – so, like many people of her generation, she’s on all the dating apps. The algorithm finds her match in Henry, who looks clean cut and kind eyed – or, at least, that’s what he seems from a very short video conversation on the phone, which breaks up due to bad signal. Paola’s sister Maria (Shaeane Jimenez) is visiting town because her and Paola’s father (Peter Butler) is going in for an operation, and warns her more trusting sibling not to accept Henry’s invitation to come to dinner at his house, away from the public gaze. Of course, Paola should have listened to her sister. The good looking guy (played by Luke Volker) turns out to have been a catfishing lure, and the real Henry (Jacques Adriaanse) looks like what you’d get if a troll mated with a slime mould. Plus, it’s actually Henry’s deranged mother, Lucille (a fantastic Dianne Simpson) who’s been writing all those courtly messages to Paola – who is soon sedated with drugged wine and wakes up about to be raped, exactly the sort of scenario your actual mother warned you about. Continue reading...

data.title: Waves Turn review – the exhausting, joyful, boring, wondrous realities of new motherhood
data.description: Josephine Ahnelt’s gentle but truthful documentary has home-movie intimacy and some incredibly touching moments As a piece of art depicting motherhood, Judith Rohrmoser’s self-portrait of breastfeeding sticks two fingers up at the tradition of the Madonna with child . In her painting, Rohrmoser’s baby feeds contentedly, chubby cheeked and sleepy under damp lashes. The artist is less serene, looking directly at us, headphones clamped over her ears, eyes filled with what might be a roar of grief, or possibly an overwhelming sense that everything has changed. Rohrmoser is one of five women who agreed to be filmed at their most vulnerable in the first year of motherhood for this Austrian documentary. It’s a gentle but truthful look at new motherhood, making the point that – ignore the Renaissance artists – having a tiny baby does not put you in perpetual state of bliss. The reality is exhaustion, joy, boredom, wonder and a rush of other feelings. Director Josephine Ahnelt shoots in 16mm, her camera up close, filming with the intimacy of a home video, cutting off heads to at one point zero in on what interests her: a mother snipping her baby’s tiny fingernails. Continue reading...

data.title: Ukrainian Lessons by Charlotte Higgins review – when art and war collide
data.description: A vivid and hopeful study of how culture endures in the midst of extreme violence Towards the end of her subtly piercing book about art in wartime, Charlotte Higgins recounts an autumn visit to Kharkiv, Ukraine’s second city, in the north-east of the country, a short drive from the Russian border. In a tranquil park, she sees a man standing in a stream, making stones balance on top of each other in a teetering tower – “a metaphor of life in that city,” she writes, “that would have seemed too obvious for a novel”. Still, as a good novelist would, Higgins doesn’t seem to beg telling details from a place so much as have them leap to her open eye and ear. The cartoons a boy is watching that fall silent in a power cut, allowing the distant boom of explosions on the frontline to be heard. A cityscape tattooed on a young poet’s arm that cuts off suddenly where skin from his leg was grafted after he was torn up by shrapnel. Cataracts of larkspur, as Higgins describes them, in a field in the frontline Donbas region, “pouring down the hill, pooling at the bottom into a great lake of blooms … Larkspur thrives on ground where there has been recent disturbance.” Continue reading...

data.title: Sunrise by Téa Obreht review – secrets and myths in the American west
data.description: Set across three interwoven timelines, this absorbing tale of an abandoned mining town explores courage, cowardice and how history is recorded Téa Obreht’s novels teem with conflicting narratives, treacherous landscapes and speculative fictions. Her 2010 prizewinning debut, The Tiger’s Wife , examined themes of death, miracles and outsider status in the midst of a fictional Balkan war. Her fourth novel, Sunrise, returns to a western frontier haunted by ghosts and stalked by outlaws, a territory Obreht first explored in her second book, Inland . It is August 2024. Nina Terzic has just jumped – or was she pushed? – from a crash-landing Cessna into a lake somewhere in the mountains of Wyoming. She manages to swim to shore. There is no sign of her boyfriend Ben, who was in the plane with her, and her phone – though miraculously intact – has no signal. Nina, a postgraduate student, was supposed to be on holiday from her job as a live-in nanny in New York. We get the feeling that her relationship with Ben might have a darker underside. Continue reading...

data.title: Dressmaker – a canvas for the creativity of dream dress design
data.description: Co-created by a developer and his sewing-obsessed partner, this design game is ‘the most technically challenging’ its lead programmer has ever made When Jonathan Hau-Yoon wanted to make something as meaningful as the environmental strategy game Terra Nil , he turned for inspiration to his longtime partner. Sabrina Becker had worn a dress she made herself to their very first date, and would have studied costume design abroad had hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (a connective tissue disorder I also have) not put those plans on hold. The pair developed a concept around the creative decisions involved in dressmaking, like trying to fit pattern pieces on to available fabric while observing the grain line (the direction of the thread in woven fabric). data.title: ‘The ultimate gamers’ mascot’: Sonic the Hedgehog at 35 – from 2D to 3D to a billion-dollar film franchise
data.description: Sonic’s creators explain how the speedy scamp has kept on running through generations as an enduring avatar of ‘attitude in the face of adversity’ One day in the early 1990s, I came home from university for the weekend and discovered that my dad had bought himself a Sega Mega Drive, bundled with a copy of Sonic the Hedgehog 2. I knew about Sega’s mascot of course. The launch of the original Sonic the Hedgehog game in 1991 was a landmark moment for the company, massively boosting the sales of its 16bit console in the west, ripping market share from the dominant Super Nintendo. While Mario was the family favourite, Sonic with his speed, attitude and brash visual energy encapsulated the edgy spirit of the early 1990s MTV culture. That weekend, Dad and I did little else but team up for daylong Sonic sessions, the game’s two-player mode letting us play cooperatively as we zoomed through those dense, beautiful play zones. Thirty-five years later, I am still a Sonic fan. There have been plenty of rough times (Sonic 06, Sonic and the Secret Rings, Sonic Free Riders – sorry, I can’t go on), but there have been plenty of good ones too. (Rush, Mania and Colors, and I have a soft spot for Sonic R, a racer developed by Traveller’s Tales, which went on to make the Lego games). Few people know this rollercoaster better than Takashi Iizuka, who worked on Sonic 3 as a designer and has been series producer for almost 20 years. When he joined Sega in 1992 he wanted to work for the company’s arcade division, but after playing the original Sonic – especially Sonic 2 – he was seduced. Continue reading...

data.title: How architect Paul Revere Williams fought racism and changed the face of Los Angeles
data.description: Creating homes for Frank Sinatra, Cary Grant and Lucille Ball made Williams a star. A trio of new exhibitions shows he belongs among the 20th century’s greats When you fly into the Los Angeles airport LAX, a spindly space-age contraption is the first thing that greets your eyes outside the window. Built in the early 1960s, the Theme Building – which once attracted travelers to its in-house restaurant, designed by Walt Disney Imagineering, towering above airfields – was built by a supergroup of architects whose structures helped define the city’s midcentury aesthetic: William Pereira, Welton Becket, Charles Luckman and Paul Revere Williams. Of these architects, Williams, the first licensed Black architect in California, arguably shaped the contours of Los Angeles most deeply. In the six decades before his death in 1980, Williams completed an estimated 3,000 structures ranging from single-family residences, commercial buildings, affordable housing projects, the Los Angeles county courthouse, a reimagining of the now-razed Ambassador hotel and opulent homes for celebrities including Frank Sinatra , Barbara Stanwyck and Lucille Ball and Desi Arnaz. Perhaps most iconic of all is the Beverly Hills hotel; Williams led its renovation, and its recognizable curlicued sign is scrawled in Williams’s own handwriting. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I’ve always been fond of hairy creatures!’ Visual effects maestro Rick Baker on a monstrously good career
data.description: Rick Baker helped define Hollywood’s creature features with his wild makeup effects skills. From Locarno, he talks Gremlins, his love of simians–  and why AI will never replace expert design When Rick Baker was 22 years old and laying the first bricks of what would become one of the great Hollywood careers, he travelled to Hatra in Iraq with director William Friedkin to assist with Max von Sydow’s makeup on The Exorcist. “Oh, he was definitely a lunatic,” Baker recalls of Friedkin, his signature goatee and ponytail still intact, if a little more salt than pepper these days. “But he made a great movie.” Friedkin had been travelling with a fake passport, and the production was plagued by extreme heat and dust storms – but the show went on. “I did von Sydow’s hands,” Baker says. “I pretty much just held a glue bottle.” We are speaking in Locarno, Switzerland, during the film festival, where Baker has accepted a lifetime achievement award and introduced screenings of An American Werewolf in London and The Nutty Professor – the first and fourth of his seven Oscar wins. When he completed his last big production, Maleficent, in 2014, it ended a more than 40-year career in which he made some huge contributions to popular culture. The monsters in Michael Jackson’s Thriller video? They were Baker’s handiwork. The Mos Eisley cantina band in Star Wars? That was him, too. In 1999, he leaked a story to the press to stop the studio from simply painting Jim Carrey green instead of using his designs for How the Grinch Stole Christmas; he won the argument and a sixth Oscar followed. Continue reading...

data.title: Laughing on the other side: the fringe shows turning painful breakups into comedy
data.description: Whether Elf Lyons’ high-concept Hollywood throwback, Kate Dehnert’s disorientating rave or Ele McKenzie’s Bob Dylan fantasy, heartbreak fuels fine humour at the festival Breakups. We’ve all been through them. Sometimes they’re mutual, sometimes not. Sometimes agony, sometimes relief. And sometimes, they’re world-shattering bereavements that seem to end, or at least upend, everything. That’s the experience two comedy shows seek to express on this year’s fringe – an experience that can’t be captured by the usual conventions of the medium. Wry wisecracks into a microphone just won’t cut it. A whole new form is required. Perhaps formal innovation isn’t such a shock when Elf Lyons is the innovator, as almost all of this dedicated nonconformist’s work has been entirely bespoke. But even for her, The Woman on the Edge is something different: shards of a disintegrating sense of self, grafted together to suggest the journey Lyons has been on since her relationship ended, shortly before her wedding day, early last year. The conceit is that the show is being performed by a Norma Desmond-alike alter ego. A brittle and wise-cracking refugee from vintage Hollywood, smoke plumes from her décolletage as she fills in for absent Elf while keeping at bay her husband, the clown Pagliacci, on the end of the phone. Continue reading...

data.description: When ovens and stovetops just won’t do, turn to loaded toasts, open sandwiches, cold noodles and smashed cucumbers, say our no-cook experts It’s too hot to turn on the oven or stove. What can I make for dinner that’s still substantial? Mark, via email This sounds like a job for Lucy Carr-Ellison, of Tart London , who is fully functioning in a no-oven household. “We moved in last year and there’s an Aga, which was amazing in winter, but we can’t have it on in summer,” she says, so toast toppers have become a crucial category of cooking: “Try rubbing toasts with garlic, adding a bit of olive oil, some grated tomatoes, lots of salt and tinned anchovies.” Otherwise, Mark could do away with the toaster and get some focaccia, suggests Jamie Pickles, chef/co-owner of Stow and The Trof , both in Manchester: “Mix picked brown crab meat with mayo, lemon juice and mustard, and spread that over the bread.” Next, combine the picked white meat with chopped chives and coriander, lemon juice, creme fraiche and black pepper. “Mix through some tinned sweetcorn, spread that over the brown crab mayo and finish with watercress.” Got a culinary dilemma? data.title: Transylvania beyond the spooky castles: a family adventure in Romania’s mountains
data.description: Forget the vampire tales – the Eastern Carpathians deliver dramatic peaks, roaming bears and deep solitude As the sun disappears behind the high tree line, our campfire spits and crackles. Four plump trout are sizzling on a flame-heated slab of rock, a cooking technique used by people in the Gurghiu mountains, part of Transylvania’s Eastern Carpathians, for centuries. Apart from gentle birdsong, it’s the only sound up here, 1,550 metres above sea level and far from any town or village. “This area is very wild,” says Samir Teslovan, who drove us up through the densely forested peaks from his guesthouse in Toplița. “When I come here to the mountains, I charge my battery, charge my soul. I feel free, like the wind.” Continue reading...

data.title: Houseplant hacks: should you always quarantine new plants to avoid pests spreading?
data.description: Any new addition to your collection can contain stowaways, so you’d be wise to deploy a little patience – but how long is long enough? The problem There is nothing quite like the joy of bringing home a new plant. You find the perfect spot, nestle it in among your others, and stand back to admire the new arrival. What you cannot see are its passengers: a few spider mites tucked under a leaf, mealybug eggs in a joint, or fungus gnat larvae in the compost. A fortnight later, plants that were perfectly healthy are speckled, sticky or swarming, and you have no idea how it happened. The hack Quarantining means keeping any new plant separated from the rest of your collection for a few weeks before letting it join the others. The logic is simple: if something is going to emerge, you want it to do so in isolation, where it can be dealt with before it spreads to the whole crew. Continue reading...

data.title: Samira’s story: the Sudanese refugee who has known no peace since she was 10
data.description: Since civil war first reached her village in 2003, Samira has been displaced seven times, enduring devastating losses and injuries along the way Every morning, she spreads small piles of rice and spices on an aluminium tray in the market of Korsi refugee camp. Some of it comes from her monthly food ration, already meagre, distributed by the UN’s World Food Programme; some she buys when she can and resells for a small profit. Samira crouches quietly behind her modest display, greeting customers as they pass. Her loose red toub cloth frames her thin face and falls across one side of it, hiding her injured right eye. Every so often she adjusts the long cloth to cover the empty sleeve where her right arm would have been. It is a habit the 33-year-old has developed since the war, but her injuries are only part of the terrible damage it has inflicted. Continue reading...

data.title: En Ukraine, l’ancien ministre de la défense Mykhaïlo Fedorov réclame la tenue d’élections et dénonce la corruption, dans un acte de défi à Volodymyr Zelensky
data.description: Le populaire ex-ministre, dont l’exclusion du gouvernement a précipité une crise politique dans le pays, franchit une ligne jamais dépassée depuis le début de l’invasion russe en appelant, dans une vidéo publiée mardi 18 août, à « restaurer le processus démocratique » malgré la guerre.
data.translatedTitle: In Ukraine, former Defense Minister Mykhaïlo Fedorov calls for elections to be held and denounces corruption, in an act of defiance to Volodymyr Zelensky
data.translatedDescription: The popular ex-minister, whose exclusion from the government precipitated a political crisis in the country, crosses a line never crossed since the start of the Russian invasion by calling, in a video published Tuesday August 18, to “restore the democratic process” despite the war.

data.title: Au procès de Meta, la firme de Mark Zuckerberg accusée d’avoir ciblé les enfants et minoré les dangers d’Instagram

data.translatedTitle: At the Meta trial, Mark Zuckerberg's firm accused of targeting children and downplaying the dangers of Instagram
data.translatedDescription: The company is on civil trial in California, sued by 29 states for having deceived consumers and violated the federal law on the protection of minors, by exposing young users to violent or sexual content and to the risk of addiction.

data.title: Le bombardement par Israël d’une base aérienne en Syrie, un avertissement à Damas et à Ankara
data.description: Alors que les négociations sur un accord de sécurité avec le nouveau pouvoir syrien sont au point mort, l’Etat hébreu a frappé un site militaire pour empêcher le pays de reconstruire sa force aérienne avec l’aide de la Turquie.
data.translatedTitle: Israel's bombing of an air base in Syria, a warning to Damascus and Ankara
data.translatedDescription: While negotiations on a security agreement with the new Syrian power are at a standstill, the Jewish state struck a military site to prevent the country from rebuilding its air force with help from Turkey.

data.title: Les exercices militaires conjoints de la Corée du Sud et des Etats-Unis écourtés de six jours, annonce Séoul après les critiques émises par Donald Trump
data.description: Ces manœuvres annuelles, qui devaient initialement durer onze jours, ont commencé lundi 17 août. Le locataire de la Maison Blanche a annoncé, dimanche, réduire la participation américaine à ces opérations, qui adressaient selon lui « un signal totalement inapproprié et hostile » à la Corée du Nord.
data.translatedTitle: Joint military exercises between South Korea and the United States cut short by six days, Seoul announces after criticism from Donald Trump
data.translatedDescription: These annual maneuvers, which were initially scheduled to last eleven days, began Monday, August 17. The White House tenant announced on Sunday that he would reduce American participation in these operations, which he said sent “a totally inappropriate and hostile signal” to North Korea.

data.title: L’aide à mourir officiellement autorisée en France après la promulgation de la loi par Emmanuel Macron
data.description: Le texte, validé par le Conseil constitutionnel avec quelques réserves, a été publié, mercredi 19 août au « Journal officiel ». Il crée un droit à l’aide à mourir, sous plusieurs conditions, pour certains patients.
data.translatedTitle: Assisted dying officially authorized in France after the promulgation of the law by Emmanuel Macron
data.translatedDescription: The text, validated by the Constitutional Council with some reservations, was published on Wednesday August 19 in the “Official Journal”. It creates a right to assistance in dying, under several conditions, for certain patients.

data.title: Frank Beard, batteur historique du groupe de rock ZZ Top, est mort à 77 ans
data.description: Seul membre du trio d’origine à ne pas avoir la barbe, Frank Beard avait dû quitter la tournée actuelle du groupe au début du mois d’août, en raison de problèmes de santé qui n’ont pas été précisés.
data.translatedTitle: Frank Beard, historic drummer for rock band ZZ Top, dies at 77
data.translatedDescription: The only member of the original trio not to have a beard, Frank Beard had to leave the group's current tour at the beginning of August, due to unspecified health problems.

data.title: Sophie Adenot est devenue la première Française à sortir dans l’espace
data.description: Agée de 44 ans, l’astronaute, en mission dans la Station spatiale internationale (ISS) depuis la mi-février, est la deuxième femme européenne à réaliser une telle sortie, après l’Italienne Samantha Cristoforetti en 2022.
data.translatedTitle: Sophie Adenot became the first French woman to go into space
data.translatedDescription: Aged 44, the astronaut, on a mission to the International Space Station (ISS) since mid-February, is the second European woman to carry out such an outing, after the Italian Samantha Cristoforetti in 2022.

data.title: Les Etats-Unis suspendent les surtaxes douanières de 50 % envers le Canada après la conclusion d’un accord
data.description: Ces nouveaux droits de douane, qui devaient entrer en vigueur mercredi matin, sont suspendus pour trois jours. Ils portaient sur l’équivalent de 20 milliards de dollars d’importations canadiennes et concernaient des produits aussi variés que le ciment, les crosses de hockey sur glace ou la bière.
data.translatedTitle: US suspends 50% tariff surcharges on Canada after reaching deal
data.translatedDescription: These new customs duties, which were to come into force Wednesday morning, are suspended for three days. They involved the equivalent of $20 billion in Canadian imports and concerned products as varied as cement, ice hockey sticks and beer.

data.title: Apple consent à respecter les règles européennes sur les marchés numériques
data.description: A l’issue de deux années d’enquêtes et de recours, le géant américain s’engage à appliquer la loi communautaire sur les marchés numériques (DMA). L’entreprise s’engage à ne plus faire obstacle aux téléchargements d’applications hors de l’Apple store.
data.translatedTitle: Apple agrees to respect European rules on digital markets
data.translatedDescription: After two years of investigations and appeals, the American giant is committed to applying the Community law on digital markets (DMA). The company is committed to no longer hindering the downloading of applications outside the Apple store.

data.title: La NASA dévoile des images du cratère formé quand l’étage supérieur d’une fusée SpaceX s’est écrasé sur la Lune

data.title: Großbritannien: Die Tragödie um den Cambridge-Professor Jason Arday
data.description: Großbritannien streitet nach dem Tod von Jason Arday über Rassismus und Plagiatsvorwürfe. Wurde er Opfer einer Hetzkampagne – oder war er ein Hochstapler? Seine nun erschienene Autobiografie wirft neue Fragen auf.

data.translatedDescription: Britain is at loggerheads over racism and plagiarism allegations following the death of Jason Arday. Was he the victim of a smear campaign – or was he an impostor? His autobiography, which has now been published, raises new questions.

data.title: Kerosinablass bei Notfall in München: Wie gefährlich ist es, wenn ein Flugzeug 60 Tonnen Treibstoff versprüht?

It is not a temporary escalation, writes Kristina Lindquist.

data.title: 18 augusti: Missa inte dagens nyheter
data.description: 14-åriga flickor gripna för skjutning i Södertälje, Stockholmsbörsen backar för tionde dagen i rad och bank-id ställer till problem när Helenas dotter behöver hjälp. Här är dagens viktigaste nyheter.
data.translatedTitle: August 18: Don't miss today's news
data.translatedDescription: 14-year-old girls arrested for shooting in Södertälje, the Stockholm stock exchange backs down for the tenth day in a row and bank ID causes problems when Helena's daughter needs help. Here are today's most important news.

data.title: Insändare. Noterat av DN:s läsare den 18 augusti
data.description: INSÄNDARE. Dagens Nyheters läsare ger sin syn på läget i Sverige och världen samt DN:s innehåll tisdagen den 18 augusti.
data.translatedTitle: Letter to the editor. Noted by DN's readers on 18 August
data.translatedDescription: LETTER TO THE EDITOR. Dagens Nyheter's readers give their views on the situation in Sweden and the world as well as DN's content on Tuesday, August 18.

data.title: Olle Hammar: Att prata om invandrares homofobi är att kasta sten i glashus
data.description: Regeringen slår larm om invandrares homofobi. Men långt in i modern tid hade svenskarna en negativ syn på homosexualitet – och än i dag sticker Kristdemokraternas och Sverigedemokraternas väljare ut, skriver forskaren Olle Hammar.
data.translatedTitle: Olle Hammar: Talking about immigrants' homophobia is throwing stones into glass houses
data.translatedDescription: The government sounds the alarm about immigrants' homophobia. But well into modern times, the Swedes had a negative view of homosexuality - and even today the voters of the Christian Democrats and the Sweden Democrats stand out, writes researcher Olle Hammar.

data.title: Melania Trump har inte synts till på en månad: ”Märkligt”
data.description: Melania Trump har gått från en undanskymd roll som presidentfru till så gott som osynlig. Trots att höstens mellanårsval närmar sig har det gått en månad sedan hennes senaste offentliga framträdande. – Det är märkligt att hon inte är med i fler sammanhang, säger USA-experten Emma Ricknell.
data.translatedTitle: Melania Trump hasn't been seen in a month: "Strange"
data.translatedDescription: Melania Trump has gone from a hidden role as First Lady to being virtually invisible. Despite the fall midterm elections approaching, it has been a month since her last public appearance. - It is strange that she is not involved in more contexts, says US expert Emma Ricknell.

data.title: Nödläget: Svensk damfotboll tappar största sponsorerna
data.description: Svensk damfotboll är i ett kritiskt läge. Varken huvudsponsorn eller titelsponsorn förlänger sina avtal med Elitfotboll dam (EFD). Samtidigt backar publiksnittet i damallsvenskan. – Vi är i ett viktigt, avgörande skede, säger EFD:s nya ordförande Ylva Johansson till DN.
data.translatedTitle: The emergency: Swedish women's football loses its biggest sponsors
data.translatedDescription: Swedish women's football is in a critical situation. Neither the main sponsor nor the title sponsor are extending their agreements with Elitfotboll dam (EFD). At the same time, the average audience in the women's league is declining. - We are at an important, decisive stage, says EFD's new chairman Ylva Johansson to DN.

data.title: DN Debatt. ”Ifrågasätt inte mitt engagemang för kvinnor – blir heligt förbannad”
data.description: DN DEBATT. Pengar är frihet, särskilt för kvinnor. Det har min mamma, farmor och mormor lärt mig. Jämställdhet är inte bara ett värdeord för politiska högtidstal. Jag invänder starkt mot olika förslag, även borgerliga sådana, som erbjuder ekonomiska plåster på såret i stället för att skapa verklig rättvisa, skriver utrikesminister Maria Malmer Stenergard (M).
data.translatedTitle: DN Debate. "Don't question my commitment to women - holy shit"
data.translatedDescription: DN DEBATE. Money is freedom, especially for women. My mother, grandmother and grandmother taught me that. Equality is not just a buzzword for political celebratory speeches. I strongly object to various proposals, even bourgeois ones, which offer financial plasters on the wound instead of creating real justice, writes Foreign Minister Maria Malmer Stenergard (M).

data.title: Flera fall av mässling – vad undrar du? Chatta med experten
data.description: Kan mässling vara farligt? Varför smittas folk nu? Spelar det någon roll om man är vaccinerad? Chatta med före detta statsepidemiologen och överläkaren Magnus Gisslén – från klockan 21. Ställ din fråga redan nu!
data.translatedTitle: Multiple cases of measles - what do you wonder? Chat with the expert
data.translatedDescription: Can measles be dangerous? Why are people infected now? Does it matter if you are vaccinated? Chat with former state epidemiologist and chief physician Magnus Gisslén - starting at 9 p.m. Ask your question now!

data.title: Svenska fångar stoppade av Estland
data.description: Ett första flygplan med svenska fångar har landat i Estland. Men många av de fångar som Sverige velat skicka till fängelset Tartu har stoppats av estländska myndigheter.
data.translatedTitle: Swedish prisoners stopped by Estonia
data.translatedDescription: A first plane with Swedish prisoners has landed in Estonia. But many of the prisoners that Sweden wanted to send to Tartu prison have been stopped by Estonian authorities.

data.title: Sanna Torén Björling: Ukrainarna tillåter ingen att inskränka deras demokrati
data.description: KIEV. När militären plötsligt mörkar och presidenten inte förklarar sina beslut blir ukrainarna förbannade. Protesterna visar att de inte tolererar att någon petar på deras demokrati de uppfattar som sin.
data.translatedTitle: Sanna Torén Björling: Ukrainians do not allow anyone to curtail their democracy
data.translatedDescription: KIEV. When the military suddenly goes dark and the president doesn't explain his decisions, Ukrainians get pissed off. The protests show that they do not tolerate anyone poking at their democracy they perceive as theirs.

data.title: Insändare. Ge äldres frågor större plats inför valet i höst
data.description: INSÄNDARE. För vår demokrati behövs större representation av äldre och mer fokus på deras frågor. Vi behöver en mer inkluderande medierapportering och mer politiskt intresse med konkreta förslag för seniorernas utmaningar, skriver Michael Bergström.
data.translatedTitle: Letter to the editor. Give older people's issues more space before the election this autumn
data.translatedDescription: LETTER TO THE EDITOR. Our democracy needs greater representation of the elderly and more focus on their issues. We need more inclusive media reporting and more political interest with concrete proposals for the seniors' challenges, writes Michael Bergström.

data.title: Irriterande, satiriskt och ibland skickligt om en kraschande konstnär
data.description: I Khashayar Lykke Naderehvandis nya roman ”Segrarens natt” möter vi en konstnär som har allt – men som börjar förlora det. Kristina Lindquist är tveksamt positiv.
data.translatedTitle: Irritating, satirical and sometimes clever about a crashing artist
data.translatedDescription: In Khashayar Lykke Naderehvandi's new novel "The Night of the Victor", we meet an artist who has everything - but is beginning to lose it. Kristina Lindquist is doubtfully positive.

data.title: Johan Nilsson: De som låter bli att vaccinera sig utsätter andra för fara
data.description: Föräldrar som inte låter vaccinera sina barn mot farliga sjukdomar utsätter sina egna barn och andra för fara. Samtidigt skyddas de av alla dem som väljer att vaccinera sig, skriver DN:s vetenskapsreporter Johan Nilsson.
data.translatedTitle: Johan Nilsson: Those who fail to vaccinate themselves put others at risk
data.translatedDescription: Parents who do not have their children vaccinated against dangerous diseases put their own children and others at risk. At the same time, they are protected by all those who choose to be vaccinated, writes DN's science reporter Johan Nilsson.

data.title: VM-klar efter allvarliga kraschen: ”Blev aldrig rädd”
data.description: AACHEN. I juli fördes hon med ambulans till sjukhuset efter en allvarig krasch under tävlingarna i Falsterbo. På torsdagen rider VM-debutanten Petronella Andersson in på hoppbanan i tyska Aachen. – Redan åtta dagar efter olyckan var mitt ansikte helt återställt, säger Andersson.
data.translatedTitle: WC-ready after serious crash: "Never got scared"
data.translatedDescription: AACHEN. In July, she was taken by ambulance to the hospital after a serious crash during the competitions in Falsterbo. On Thursday, WC debutant Petronella Andersson rides onto the show jumping course in Aachen, Germany. - Just eight days after the accident, my face was completely restored, says Andersson.

data.title: Sverige, Sverige, Sverige – har alla blivit nationalister inför valet?
data.description: Tonläget skruvas upp. Landet har tapetserats med valaffischer och valrörelsens först apartiledardebatt har hållits. Vad vill partierna ha för image om de själva får bestämma?
data.translatedTitle: Sweden, Sweden, Sweden - has everyone become nationalist before the election?
data.translatedDescription: The tone is turned up. The country has been wallpapered with election posters and the election movement's first party leader debate has been held. What kind of image do the parties want if they get to decide for themselves?

data.title: Uppstoppad räv var utdöd tasmansk tiger: ”Trodde de skulle svimma”
data.description: Ett uppstoppat rävhuvud som nyligen såldes på auktion i England har skapat chockvågor bland forskare och samlare. Orsaken: Det visade sig vara ett sällsynt exemplar av den utdöda tasmanska tigern.
data.translatedTitle: Stuffed fox was extinct Tasmanian tiger: "Thought they would pass out"
data.translatedDescription: A stuffed fox head recently sold at auction in England has sent shockwaves through researchers and collectors. The reason: It turned out to be a rare specimen of the extinct Tasmanian tiger.

data.title: Lisa Magnusson: Alla missar den riktiga skandalen med Fröken Snusk och SD
data.description: Samarbetet mellan Fröken Snusk och Sverigedemokraterna har väckt stor uppståndelse. Men fokus ligger på helt fel sak.
data.translatedTitle: Lisa Magnusson: Everyone misses the real scandal with Miss Snusk and SD
data.translatedDescription: The collaboration between Miss Snusk and the Sweden Democrats has caused quite a stir. But the focus is on the wrong thing.

data.title: Vita huset till angrepp mot journalist efter konflikt med Trump
data.description: Vita huset gick till angrepp på sociala medier mot en CNN-journalist efter att hon ställt en fråga till presidenten som beskrevs som oförskämd.
data.translatedTitle: White House to attack journalist after conflict with Trump
data.translatedDescription: The White House went on the offensive on social media against a CNN journalist after she asked the president a question that was described as rude.

data.title: Vem är Natalie Harp – Trumps mystiska hjälpreda?
data.description: WASHINGTON. Ingen tillbringar mer tid med USA:s president Donald Trump än Natalie Harp, 34. Assistenten har vuxit fram som en dold makthavare i Vita huset. Efter pressekreteraren Karoline Leavitts avhopp är hon en av få kvinnor i presidentens närmaste krets.
data.translatedTitle: Who is Natalie Harp - Trump's mysterious aide?
data.translatedDescription: WASHINGTON. No one spends more time with US President Donald Trump than Natalie Harp, 34. The aide has emerged as a hidden power in the White House. After the resignation of press secretary Karoline Leavitt, she is one of the few women in the president's closest circle.

data.title: Israel bombar Syrien som en varning till Turkiet
data.description: JERUSALEM. Israels flygattack på tisdagsmorgonen mot det syriska flygfältet Abu al-Duhur var en varning till den syriska regimen att inte låta Turkiet skaffa sig flygbaser där. Bombningarna fördömdes av USA:s Turkiet-ambassadör Tom Barrack, som sköter Vita Husets kontakter med den syriska regimen.
data.translatedTitle: Israel bombs Syria as a warning to Turkey
data.translatedDescription: JERUSALEM. Israel's air strike on Tuesday morning against the Syrian Abu al-Duhur airfield was a warning to the Syrian regime not to allow Turkey to acquire air bases there. The bombings were condemned by US Ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack, who manages the White House's contacts with the Syrian regime.

data.title: Trump: Inga samtal på gång med Iran
data.description: Avsiktsförklaringen mellan USA och Iran har löpt ut, men länderna förhandlar inte om ett framtida fredsavtal. ”Inga samtal pågår” skriver Donald Trump och hävdar att Hormuzsundet är öppet. Irans chefsförhandlare Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf understryker å sin sida att sundet förblir stängt.
data.translatedTitle: Trump: No talks underway with Iran
data.translatedDescription: The declaration of intent between the US and Iran has expired, but the countries are not negotiating a future peace agreement. "No talks are ongoing" writes Donald Trump and claims that the Strait of Hormuz is open. For his part, Iran's chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf emphasizes that the strait remains closed.

data.title: Äldre nekas boende – anhöriga förstår inte varför
data.description: Många äldre nekas plats på äldreboende. Samtidigt har anhöriga svårt att förstå varför. Forskare vid Stockholms universitet beskriver ett system som upplevs som både otydligt och tungrott.
data.translatedTitle: The elderly are denied accommodation – relatives do not understand why
data.translatedDescription: Many elderly people are denied a place in nursing homes. At the same time, relatives have difficulty understanding why. Researchers at Stockholm University describe a system that is perceived as both unclear and unwieldy.

data.title: Träningsformen soft wellness fortsätter växa: ”En återställare”
data.description: Soft wellness blir allt mer populärt. Istället för högintensiva pass fokuserar man mer på lågintensiv träning med mjuka och lugna rörelser. – Folk är stressade och utbrända, då behövs det här, säger Brian van den Brink, chef för träningsutveckling och utbud på Friskis & Svettis.
data.translatedTitle: The exercise form soft wellness continues to grow: "A restorer"
data.translatedDescription: Soft wellness is becoming increasingly popular. Instead of high-intensity sessions, the focus is more on low-intensity training with soft and calm movements. - People are stressed and burnt out, then this is needed, says Brian van den Brink, head of training development and supply at Friskis & Svettis.

data.title: Flera av de som smittats av mässling är barn
data.description: Elva fall av mässling har konstaterats runt om i landet. Utbrottet härleds till festivalen Urkult i Näsåker, i Sollefteå kommun. I Västerbottens län har en vuxen och ett barn smittats. – De har inte någon relation till varandra, deras gemensamma nämnare är de har besökt festivalen, säger Maria Marklund, smittskyddsläkare i Region Västerbotten.
data.translatedTitle: Several of those infected with measles are children
data.translatedDescription: Eleven cases of measles have been confirmed around the country. The outbreak is traced to the festival Urkult in Näsåker, in Sollefteå municipality. In Västerbotten County, an adult and a child have been infected. - They have no relation to each other, their common denominator is that they have visited the festival, says Maria Marklund, infectious disease doctor in Region Västerbotten.

data.title: Insändare. Jag längtar tillbaka till tidningar i fullt format
data.description: INSÄNDARE. I dagstidningar i det gamla, fullstora formatet fanns så mycket att läsa om så många olika ämnen. Det skulle kännas fint att få bläddra i en DN tryckt före tabloid­formatet, skriver Gunnar Britse.
data.translatedTitle: Letter to the editor. I long to return to full-format newspapers
data.translatedDescription: LETTER TO THE EDITOR. There was so much to read on so many different subjects in the old, full-size dailies. It would feel nice to browse through a DN printed before the tabloid format, writes Gunnar Britse.

data.title: Kriminolog: Det driver unga tjejer att begå kontraktsmord
data.description: Antalet unga flickor som tar på sig uppdraget att utföra beställningsmord är fortfarande litet – men de blir allt fler. Enligt kriminologen Sven Granath har tjejer och killar liknande drivkrafter till att begå våldsdåd. – Kanske har man överskattat könets makt här, att det på något vis skulle sitta i generna.
data.translatedTitle: Criminologist: It drives young girls to commit contract killings
data.translatedDescription: The number of young girls who take it upon themselves to carry out contract killings is still small - but they are increasing. According to criminologist Sven Granath, girls and boys have similar motivations to commit acts of violence. - Perhaps the power of gender has been overestimated here, that it would somehow be in the genes.

data.title: Insändare. Dra tillbaka beslutet att lägga ner Kunskapskanalen
data.description: INSÄNDARE. Public service har en uppsjö av hjärndöd så kallad underhållning att välja ifrån om de vill reducera sina kostnader. Tänk om, SVT, och dra tillbaka beslutet att lägga ner Kunskapskanalen.
data.translatedTitle: Letter to the editor. Withdraw the decision to close the Knowledge Channel
data.translatedDescription: LETTER TO THE EDITOR. Public service has a plethora of brain dead so-called entertainment to choose from if they want to reduce their costs. Think again, SVT, and retract the decision to shut down the Knowledge Channel.

data.title: Ukrainas kulturella styrkor vill bygga moral med musik
data.description: KIEV. Violinisten Olha Rukavisjnikova har förlorat ena ögat i strid och har splitter kvar i nacken. Nu tillhör hon Ukrainas kulturella styrkor där inkallade kulturarbetare uppträder för soldaterna vid fronten och turnerar internationellt. – När jag spelar i New York eller i Cannes får publiken en känslomässig upplevelse. De förstår vad vi går igenom – och de kan ge Ukraina sitt stöd.
data.translatedTitle: Ukraine's cultural forces want to build morale with music
data.translatedDescription: KIEV. Violinist Olha Rukavishnikova has lost one eye in battle and has shrapnel left in her neck. Now she belongs to the cultural forces of Ukraine where conscripted cultural workers perform for the soldiers at the front and tour internationally. - When I play in New York or in Cannes, the audience gets an emotional experience. They understand what we are going through - and they can support Ukraine.

data.title: Bröt mot kontaktförbud mot Frida Karlsson – åtalas igen
data.description: Mannen som tidigare dömts för att ha stalkat skidstjärnan Frida Karlsson åtalas igen. Han ska ha brutit mot kontaktförbudet genom att ringa och skicka meddelanden till Karlsson, uppger nyhetsbyrån Siren.
data.translatedTitle: Breached a contact ban against Frida Karlsson - prosecuted again
data.translatedDescription: The man who was previously convicted of stalking ski star Frida Karlsson is charged again. He is said to have violated the contact ban by calling and sending messages to Karlsson, according to the Siren news agency.

data.title: Fjäril av ”helveteslarven” har tagit sig till Sverige
data.description: Ekprocessionsspinnaren som plågat Danmark i sommar har nu tagit sig över sundet. Zooekologen Lars Pettersson på Lunds universitet bekräftar att detta är det första fallet på tolv år. – En klok sak är att för säkerhets skull inte klappa några håriga larver, säger han.
data.translatedTitle: Butterfly of the "hellworm" has made its way to Sweden
data.translatedDescription: The oak processionary spinner that plagued Denmark this summer has now crossed the strait. Zooecologist Lars Pettersson at Lund University confirms that this is the first case in twelve years. - A wise thing is not to pet any hairy caterpillars, just to be safe, he says.

data.title: Kristofer Ahlström: Vill politikerna – på riktigt – dö för sitt land?
data.description: I valspurten verkar alla politiker redo att offra sig vid fronten. Men menar de verkligen allvar? Eller försöker de rädda sitt eget skinn? DN:s Kristofer Ahlström tittar på en nypatriotisk partiledardebatt.
data.translatedTitle: Kristofer Ahlström: Do the politicians - really - want to die for their country?
data.translatedDescription: In the run-up to the election, all politicians seem ready to sacrifice themselves at the front. But are they really serious? Or are they trying to save their own skin? DN's Kristofer Ahlström watches a neo-patriotic party leader debate.

data.title: Körde ihjäl 14-årig flicka på övergångsställe – döms till rättspsykiatrisk vård
data.description: Mannens vansinnesfärd genom centrala Malmö slutade med att han körde ihjäl en 14-årig flicka på ett övergångsställe. Samma dag hade mannen flera gånger sökt vård på psykakuten och lämnat in sitt körkort. På tisdagen dömdes han till rättspsykiatrisk vård med särskild utskrivningsprövning.
data.translatedTitle: Killed 14-year-old girl at a pedestrian crossing - sentenced to forensic psychiatric care
data.translatedDescription: The man's mad journey through central Malmö ended with him killing a 14-year-old girl at a pedestrian crossing. On the same day, the man had sought treatment at the psychiatric ward several times and handed in his driver's license. On Tuesday, he was sentenced to forensic psychiatric care with a special discharge examination.

data.title: DN Debatt Repliker. ”Bara en del av de rikastes inkomster syns i deklarationen”
data.description: DN DEBATT SLUTREPLIK. Nationalekonomerna Marius Ring, David Seim och Gabriel Zucman: Vår uppgift som forskare är att visa hur systemet faktiskt fungerar.
data.translatedTitle: DN Debate Replicas. "Only part of the income of the richest is visible in the declaration"
data.translatedDescription: DN DEBATE CLOSING REMARKS. National economists Marius Ring, David Seim and Gabriel Zucman: Our task as researchers is to show how the system actually works.

data.title: Oavbrutet intressant om hur den extrema kampsporten hamnade i Trumps ringhörna
data.description: MMA har vuxit från blodig subkultur till global miljardindustri – med Donald Trump, högerextremister och auktoritära ledare i sitt följe. I ”Fight! Fight! Fight!” följer Jonas Cullberg med driv och saklighet pengarna och politiken bakom en av världens snabbast växande sporter.
data.translatedTitle: Nonstop interesting about how the extreme martial arts ended up in Trump's ring corner
data.translatedDescription: MMA has grown from bloody subculture to global billion-dollar industry - with Donald Trump, right-wing extremists and authoritarian leaders in tow. In "Fight! Fight! Fight!" Jonas Cullberg follows the money and politics behind one of the world's fastest growing sports with drive and objectivity.

data.title: Storasyster Hellvig inför hemma-EM: ”Min tur nu”
data.description: För första gången någonsin arrangeras volleyboll-EM för damer i Sverige. Hanna Hellvig ska tillsammans med det svenska laget skapa volleybollfeber i Sverige – och kanske ta över facklan i familjen. – Det kanske är min tur nu, jag får ta över det här från brorsan, säger hon och skrattar.
data.translatedTitle: Big sister Hellvig before the home EC: "My turn now"
data.translatedDescription: For the first time ever, the women's volleyball European Championship is being held in Sweden. Hanna Hellvig, together with the Swedish team, will create volleyball fever in Sweden - and perhaps take over the torch in the family. - Maybe it's my turn now, I get to take over this from my brother, she says and laughs.

data.title: Guide: Historiskt hemma-EM i volleyboll
data.description: Volleyboll-EM för damer ska för första gången spelas i Sverige. I Göteborg ska Isabelle Haak och det svenska landslaget skapa volleybollfeber. Här är allt du behöver veta inför mästerskapet.
data.translatedTitle: Guide: Historic home EC in volleyball
data.translatedDescription: The Women's Volleyball European Championship will be played in Sweden for the first time. In Gothenburg, Isabelle Haak and the Swedish national team will create volleyball fever. Here's everything you need to know ahead of the championship.

data.title: Experter: Därför har börsen backat tio dagar i rad
data.description: Stockholmsbörsen backade för tionde dagen i rad på tisdagen. En ovanlig syn. Men experterna är inte oroade. – Det är en pyspunka vi ser, säger börsstrategen Elin Benjaminsson.
data.translatedTitle: Experts: That's why the stock market has retreated ten days in a row
data.translatedDescription: The Stockholm stock exchange retreated for the tenth day in a row on Tuesday. An unusual sight. But the experts are not worried. - We are seeing a slouch, says stock market strategist Elin Benjaminsson.

data.title: Michael Winiarski: Polska högerns spricka kan missgynna Donald Tusk
data.description: Polens nationalkonservativa oppositionsparti Lag och rättvisa har splittrats. Följden är att det största partiet på högerkanten tappar sin roll som ledare för oppositionen mot Donald Tusks liberala regering. Men det förbättrar sannolikt utsikterna för extremhögern inför parlamentsvalet hösten 2027.
data.translatedTitle: Michael Winiarski: The crack in the Polish right could disadvantage Donald Tusk
data.translatedDescription: Poland's national conservative opposition Law and Justice party has split. The consequence is that the largest party on the right loses its role as leader of the opposition against Donald Tusk's liberal government. But it likely improves the prospects for the extreme right before the parliamentary elections in autumn 2027.

data.title: Flera bank-id-problem när dottern behöver hjälp
data.description: Fler vittnar om problem när e-legitimation blivit en allt större del av vardagen. Helena Dal, mamma till Mimmi som har en intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, stöter ofta på praktiska hinder med bank-id. – Det här är ett digitalt utanförskap som är mycket problematiskt.
data.translatedTitle: Several bank ID problems when the daughter needs help
data.translatedDescription: More testify to problems when e-identification has become an increasingly large part of everyday life. Helena Dal, mother of Mimmi who has an intellectual disability, often encounters practical obstacles with bank ID. - This is a digital exclusion that is very problematic.

data.title: Guide: Siffrorna du behöver ha koll på för att tona håret hemma
data.description: Har ditt hår missfärgats i sommar, silverschampot slutat hjälpa och du vill inte lägga flera tusen kronor hos frisören? Då rekommenderar frisören Nina Lind hemmatoning och guidar i fem steg till hur du hittar din perfekta nyans i sifferdjungeln på förpackningarna.
data.translatedTitle: Guide: The numbers you need to keep track of toning your hair at home
data.translatedDescription: Has your hair discolored this summer, the silver shampoo stopped helping and you don't want to spend several thousand kroner at the hairdresser? Then hairdresser Nina Lind recommends home toning and guides in five steps how to find your perfect shade in the jungle of numbers on the packages.

data.title: Skjuten pojke inte livshotande skadad – 14-åringar gripna
data.description: En 17-årig pojke blev skjuten vid en skola i Södertälje på måndagen – och två 14-åriga flickor greps kort efteråt. Pojken är inte livshotande skadad, uppger polisen.
data.translatedTitle: Boy shot not life-threateningly injured - 14-year-olds arrested
data.translatedDescription: A 17-year-old boy was shot at a school in Södertälje on Monday - and two 14-year-old girls were arrested shortly afterwards. The boy's injuries are not life-threatening, the police say.

data.title: Insändare. Sänk straffbarhetsåldern till 10 år
data.description: INSÄNDARE. I ett rättssamhälle är det rimligt att de som begår grova brott erhåller någon form av konsekvens för sina handlingar, oavsett ålder. Ju tidigare samhället ingriper, desto bättre, skriver Jan Lindman.
data.translatedTitle: Letter to the editor. Lower the age of criminal liability to 10 years

data.translatedTitle: What has been done about women's safety a year after the murder of seventeen-year-old Lisa? 'You have to draw attention to this on a structural basis, not just during high-profile events'

data.title: Is de mysterieuze figuur die niet kan communiceren vanwege een stoornis Chris de Canadees? Of de boeddhistische Lucky? Of eigenlijk toch Lee?

De politie verspreidt deze week zijn signalement, hopend op nieuwe aanwijzingen. „Het was wel een geheimschrijver, he.”
data.translatedTitle: Is the mysterious figure who cannot communicate due to a disorder Chris the Canadian? Or the Buddhist Lucky? Or actually Lee?

data.description: De narwal is het enige zoogdier met een vrijwel kaarsrechte slagtand, zo ongewoon dat hij de mythe van de eenhoorn inspireerde. Dankzij minutieus wetenschappelijk onderzoek is nu bevestigd dat de tand een spiraalgroei in tegengestelde richtingen kent, oftewel een dubbele helix.
data.translatedTitle: The narwhal's tusk grows exceptionally straight thanks to its special spiral growth
data.translatedDescription: The narwhal is the only mammal with an almost straight tusk, so unusual that it inspired the myth of the unicorn. Thanks to meticulous scientific research, it has now been confirmed that the tooth has spiral growth in opposite directions, or a double helix.

data.title: De politie in Twente wil trekkers van de snelweg weren. Hoe vallen de boeren te stoppen?
data.description: Burgemeesters in de regio Twente zullen in het vervolg optreden tegen trekkers op de snelweg. Maar hoe? Over de uitvoering wordt verschillend gedacht. „Je zou hopen dat de politie meer shovels heeft aangeschaft.”
data.translatedTitle: The police in Twente want to ban tractors from the highway. How can the farmers be stopped?
data.translatedDescription: Mayors in the Twente region will take action against tractors on the highway in the future. But how? There are different opinions about the implementation. “You would hope that the police would have purchased more shovels.”

data.title: VS gaven razendsnel 100 miljard aan heffingen terug, maar openen tegelijk een nieuw front in de handelsoorlog
data.description: In recordtempo is de Amerikaanse douane bezig om bedrijven illegaal geïnde heffingen terug te betalen. Tegelijkertijd wil Trump landen die China helpen harder aanpakken, onder meer met „een grensbewaker die nooit slaapt”.
data.translatedTitle: The US quickly refunded 100 billion in tariffs, but at the same time opened a new front in the trade war
data.translatedDescription: US Customs is working in record time to refund companies illegally collected duties. At the same time, Trump wants to crack down on countries that help China, including with "a border guard that never sleeps."

data.description: Wereldzaken is met vakantie, maar we zijn niet helemaal weg. In de tussentijd kan je luisteren naar onze zomerselectie: vier van onze beste afleveringen van het afgelopen jaar.
data.translatedTitle: Summer selection: The power of geography: can mountain ranges predict wars?
data.translatedDescription: World Affairs is on holiday, but we are not completely gone. In the meantime, you can listen to our summer selection: four of our best episodes from the past year.

data.translatedTitle: “Is everything okay there?”
